This trade summary feeds the Budget and Payment Claim tabs.
No.Cost CodeTradeBudgetApproved VOsBudget TransferRevised BudgetCommittedSub VOsPending POsFC CompleteTotal FCGain/Loss
Budget, Approved VOs, Revised Budget, Committed Cost, Subcontract VOs and Pending POs are all automatic figures: Budget from each trade's value on Trade Summary (or the Preliminaries & General total); Committed Cost from Engaged/Complete subcontractors' contract sums plus closed Purchase Orders' invoiced amounts against the matching cost code; Subcontract VOs from that subcontractor's approved variations; Pending POs from the ordered value of open Purchase Orders against the matching cost code (see the Purchasing tab). Budget Transfer is the net of every completed transfer against that cost code — the only way money moves from one cost code to another; use the "Budget Transfer" button above to record one. Forecast to Complete is the only figure you set by hand — click its value to open that cost code's own Item / Description / Duration / Qty / Rate worksheet and build it up there; leave the worksheet empty to keep the automatic figure. Use "+ Add line item" for costs that don't come from a priced trade. Trade names and cost codes are fixed here — set them on Tender Analysis or the Preliminaries & General worksheet. Click "Lock Budget" once pricing is finalised to prevent further changes (Forecast to Complete and Budget Transfer stay available); unlocking again needs the project PIN.

Budget Transfer Register

Every transfer of budget from one cost code to another, in the order recorded. This is the only way money moves between cost codes on the Budget. Use Edit or Delete on a row to correct or remove one.

Task Analysis (TA)

Task Analysis / Safe Work Method Statement Sign-on

All workers must sign this register to show that they have been involved in the processes and will work to the requirements of this TA/SWMS.

Worker Name Worker Signature

Sequence of Steps, Hazards & Controls

Describe each step in the activity — most will have 4–8 steps, following the flow of the product or process. List the potential hazards and risks for each step (there will normally be more than one), the initial risk before controls are in place (refer to the Risk Assessment Matrix), the control method and level of control (refer to the Hierarchy of Controls), and the residual risk once all controls are in place.
